name: use-omp-manual-invocation
reason: OMP exposes hidden skills through its native /skill:<name> command.

name: run-with-explicit-dependencies
reason: Use the shipped TypeScript entry on Windows without a POSIX launcher or an implicit host installation.
anchor:
```sh
<skill dir>/scripts/statechart SPEC.tla [--config FILE] [--view FILE] [--out DIR]
```

`scripts/statechart.ts` is TypeScript, so run it with a runtime that can execute TypeScript. `scripts/statechart` is a POSIX shell script that picks one. On native Windows, run `node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning <skill dir>/scripts/statechart.ts` with Node 22.18 to 22.x, or Node 23.6 or later.

The first run installs TLC and Java with mise and needs the network.
replace:
```sh
bun "<skill dir>/scripts/statechart.ts" SPEC.tla [--config FILE] [--view FILE] [--out DIR]
```

Use Bun 1.4.4, an existing Java runtime (Java 11 or later; Windows exercised with Oracle JDK 26), and the official [TLA+ Tools 1.7.4](https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/tag/v1.7.4) `tla2tools.jar` (TLC 2.19, revision `5a47802`). The jar SHA-256 is `936a262061c914694dfd669a543be24573c45d5aa0ff20a8b96b23d01e050e88`. Set `TLA2TOOLS` to the jar's absolute path and optionally `JAVA` to the Java executable's absolute path (default: `java` on PATH). The command does not download or install dependencies. On Windows these are ordinary environment variables (for example, `$env:TLA2TOOLS = 'C:\path\to\tla2tools.jar'` in PowerShell). A rule violation writes a chart and report but exits 1; an execution or input error exits 2 without publishing output.
